text: EU AI Act Article 50, measured: the reassurance gap | CSOAI Home Blog EU AI Act Article 50, measured: the reassurance gap 2026-08-08 · CSOAI The EU AI Act Article 50 transparency rules are live. What they require in practice is ordinary human reassurance : can I tell, when I meet an AI-generated artifact, that it was AI-generated, and by whom? The regulation is about marking and disclosure — and the market's real demand is not a certification certificate, it is the ability to reassure a counterparty that the provenance is checkable. What our measurement shows CSOAI tests AI systems against 417 statutory provisions crosswalked across the EU, UK and US, and signs every result so it can be verified offline. The working instrument for Article 50 is the free signed passport . The reason a passport works where a white-paper does not: each claim traces to a signed, recompute-able record. Why this is the product For an exporter, complying is table stakes. Being able to prove what you measured is the difference between a compliance statement and a defensible one. That is the reassurance gap we measure and close. CSOAI Ltd · UK 16939677 · Every published figure traces to a signed, verifiable record.
